### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/README.md`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via startedAt (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileReport))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via /:object/:id/shares (route, bridged from symbol sourceId — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via sourceId (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeReconcileEntry), /:object/:id/shares (route, bridged from symbol sourceId — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/README.md`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57ab08760c7ffd506454864b22c0ce7d9a614164` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d13e70081295f30c91b57dc1292de3141adc0b3d` — the merge of head `e239d4b1bac0d9ad964d0e6e5feb26a26f449dd9` into base `57ab08760c7ffd506454864b22c0ce7d9a614164`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d13e70081295f30c91b57dc1292de3141adc0b3d && git checkout d13e70081295f30c91b57dc1292de3141adc0b3d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57ab08760c7ffd506454864b22c0ce7d9a614164 e239d4b1bac0d9ad964d0e6e5feb26a26f449dd9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57ab08760c7ffd506454864b22c0ce7d9a614164 && git merge --no-ff e239d4b1bac0d9ad964d0e6e5feb26a26f449dd9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57ab08760c7ffd506454864b22c0ce7d9a614164
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57ab08760c7ffd506454864b22c0ce7d9a614164` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `e239d4b1bac0d9ad964d0e6e5feb26a26f449dd9` (Fixes #37734). Full read · 2026-11-27T14:25Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** 12 files, +1315/-80. Check-runs at e239d4b1, re-read live: 40 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed, none pending (Test Core 5/10 has finished); mergeable_state clean. Not governed (0 of 12 paths). `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. No adapter-contract member is added (K10). The plugin option and the `reconcile` trigger land with their readers.

**The card's items, read against the code.**
- **The pass.** `reconcileSources()` runs passes one after another on a `reconcileTail` chain. Each source goes through the existing `rebuildOf(entry, { trigger: 'reconcile' })`, so there is no second walk and no second purge. A source re-registered mid-pass is skipped by the `byIndexKey(entry.key) !== entry` check. A throw becomes a `failed` record rather than ending the pass.
- **Which sources.** `reconcileExclusion` leaves out `onRecordChange: false`, no data engine, and an adapter without `listDocuments`. The last is said once per source at `warn`, naming `os knowledge rebuild`. A source whose adapter is not mounted is still walked and fails with the coded 503, so the daily run reads `degraded` naming it. I read that as the right signal.
- **Point 1, the post-lock due check.** It is now limited to `boot` and `reload` (it was `!== 'operator'`), so a reconcile walks a current source completely, like an operator rebuild. The skip keeps that free of embedding. That is the card's item 1. The index-state reading still runs before the walk and logs when the source is due.
- **The schedule.** One `knowledge:reconcile` cron job on `IJobService`, `'0 3 * * *'` UTC by default, moved by `{ cron, timezone }`, off with `false`. A refused cron, an unreadable job service and a missing job service are each said once. Stopping the plugin cancels the job. `reconcileJobOutcome` answers `degraded` naming each unfinished source, else `completed`, which the job adapters record as success.
- **After a predicate write.** There is one timer per index key, re-armed by each write, waiting 2 min of quiet and at most 10 min after the first write. A running build re-arms the timer instead of queuing behind it. The timer is unref'd, and removal and stop cancel it.

**Point 2, debug for an object no source indexes: accepted.** The old `warn` fired on every predicate write to any object, which was noise where nothing is indexed. It is declared in the PR. Under `reconcile: false` the old sentence is kept word for word, and the one edited test now registers a source whose adapter cannot list documents, so it still pins the stale-index warning where no reconcile can repair it.

**Point 3, live PG skipped in CI:** the standing state for pgvector live cells (Temporal Conformance never runs on a PR), not this PR's gap. The local PG16 + pgvector reading counts.

**Point 4, the unlocked narrowed re-run after the merge: accepted.** The merge brought #37942's pgvector adapter change, which is exactly what the new live purge case touches, and the dev re-ran all 10 knowledge-pgvector files on live PG at the final head, 97/97. The memory reconcile file and the three service-knowledge files most exposed to the merge were re-run too. The full suites at `c771dc877a` plus Test Core 10/10 on the head cover the rest.

**Acceptance, case by case.** Each row of the card has a named case: the one-reconcile convergence (insert, change, predicate delete, out of `where`) with a second reconcile that embeds 0; the outage convergence; ten predicate writes starting one reconcile, plus the 10-minute cap; the unlisted adapter and `onRecordChange: false`; the moved fingerprint built as a new generation; two nodes with one `not-run`; lease lost; `degraded` and `success`; `reconcile: false`; no job service; and the rolled-back insert. The PostgreSQL purge case is the card's item 5. Nine ablations each turn the matching cases red, and the container run shows the job scheduled at boot.

**Docs and changeset, sentence by sentence.** `knowledge.mdx`'s new section, the predicate-write and stale-document edits, `knowledge-rag.mdx`'s daily-reconcile paragraph and fingerprint sentence, and the README paragraph all match the code: the trigger, the four repairs, what is walked, the third index-state reading, 03:00 UTC, the option, `degraded`, the once-said lines, and the in-memory record. The stores named as listing their documents (pgvector, Turso, memory) each implement `listDocuments`. The changeset's bullets match the code and the new exports. `patch` is right for `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**Landing:** not governed, no narrowing. The area lands it. The diff is 1,395 lines, under the 3000 limit.
